s:
Match List-I with List-II with reference to the Committees of the Constituent Assembly:

List-I (Committee)
a. Rules of Procedure Committee
b. Advisory Committee
c. Drafting Committee
d. House Committee

List-II (Chairman)
i. B.R. Ambedkar
ii. Vallabhbhai Patel
iii. Rajendra Prasad
iv. B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: The Rules of Procedure Committee was chaired by Rajendra Prasad, the Advisory Committee by Vallabhbhai Patel, the Drafting Committee by B.R. Ambedkar and the House Committee by B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya.
tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped chairman.

s: Who among the following chaired the Committee on Order of Business of the Constituent Assembly?
x: The Committee on Order of Business was chaired by K.M. Munshi.
tq: Use the chairman–committee association directly rather than confusing it with the Credentials Committee.

s:
Consider the following pairs:

1. Finance and Staff Committee — Rajendra Prasad
2. States Committee — Jawaharlal Nehru
3. Credentials Committee — Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar
4. Union Constitution Committee — Vallabhbhai Patel

Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
x: Pairs 1, 2 and 3 are correctly matched. The Union Constitution Committee was chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru, not Vallabhbhai Patel.
tq: Find the swapped chairman in the final pair before selecting the coded combination.

s:
Match the following sub-committees of the Constituent Assembly with their chairmen:

List-I
 a. Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee
 b. Minorities Sub-Committee
 c. North-East Frontier Tribal Areas Sub-Committee
 d. Excluded Areas Sub-Committee other than Assam

List-II
 i. Gopinath Bardoloi
 ii. J.B. Kripalani
 iii. A.V. Thakkar
 iv. H.C. Mukherjee

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: J.B. Kripalani chaired the Fundamental Rights Sub-Committee, H.C. Mukherjee the Minorities Sub-Committee, Gopinath Bardoloi the North-East Frontier Tribal Areas Sub-Committee and A.V. Thakkar the other excluded areas sub-committee.
tq: Match each sub-committee with its specialist chair; eliminate by the repeated sure pairs.

s: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on
x: The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949. It came into full effect on 26 January 1950.
tq: Distinguish the adoption date from the signing date and the commencement date.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s:
Which of the following provisions came into force on 26 November 1949 along with the adoption of the Constitution?

1. Provisions relating to citizenship
2. Provisions relating to elections
3. Provisions relating to the provisional Parliament
4. All provisions of the Constitution

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Citizenship, elections, the provisional Parliament and transitional provisions came into force on 26 November 1949. The remaining provisions commenced on 26 January 1950.
tq: Watch for the absolute statement that all provisions commenced on the adoption date.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s: Which one of the following sets contains only provisions that took effect on 26 November 1949?
x: The provisions relating to citizenship, the oath of the President, elections, definitions and interpretation, including Articles 5–9, 60, 324, 366 and 367, took effect on 26 November 1949.
tq: Group the provisions by their commencement date instead of relying on article-number familiarity.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s: The Constituent Assembly took approximately how long to complete its work?
x: The Constituent Assembly completed its work in 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.
tq: Use the distinctive middle-value date-duration combination as the identifying figure.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the working of the Constituent Assembly:

1. It held 11 sessions.
2. It sat for 165 days.
3. The Draft Constitution was discussed for 114 days.
4. It consulted about 60 constitutions.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements are correct: the Assembly held 11 sessions, sat for 165 days, discussed the draft for 114 days and consulted about 60 constitutions.
tq: Check each numerical statement independently before selecting the complete combination.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s: The approximate cost incurred in framing the Constitution of India was
x: The Constitution-making process cost approximately Rs. 64 lakh.
tq: Separate the cost figure from the nearby figures relating to time, sessions and days.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s: Which of the following correctly represents the original Constitution of India?
x: The original Constitution contained 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
tq: Keep the original structure separate from the approximate present structure.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s: As compared with the original Constitution, the Constitution of India at present has approximately
x: The Constitution presently has approximately 470 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules, as compared with the original 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules.
tq: Use the comparison direction carefully: original figures are not the approximate current figures.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s: The members of the Constituent Assembly signed the Constitution on
x: The Constitution was signed by 284 members on 24 January 1950.
tq: Discriminate among adoption, signing and commencement dates.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s: Why was 26 January chosen as the date for the commencement of the Constitution?
o: It was the date of the Cabinet Mission Plan.
It marked the Purna Swaraj declaration and its first observance in 1930.
It commemorated the first meeting of the Constituent Assembly.
It was the date on which the Indian Independence Act was passed.
x: 26 January was chosen to honour Purna Swaraj Day, first celebrated on 26 January 1930 pursuant to the Lahore Congress resolution of December 1929.
tq: Link the commencement date with the national movement event it was intended to commemorate.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s:
Consider the following statements:

1. Constitution Day is observed on 26 November.
2. Constitution Day has been observed since 2015.
3. The declaration of Constitution Day in 2015 coincided with the 125th birth-anniversary year of B.R. Ambedkar.
4. Republic Day is observed on 26 November.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Republic Day is observed on 26 January, not on 26 November.
tq: Identify the reversed-date trap between Constitution Day and Republic Day.
sec: Adoption and commencement - dates, time, sessions, 26 January, Constitution Day

s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:

A. Adoption of the Constitution
B. First sitting of the Constituent Assembly
C. Election of Rajendra Prasad as permanent President
D. Signing of the Constitution by the members
x: The first sitting was on 9 December 1946, Rajendra Prasad was elected on 11 December 1946, the Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and signed on 24 January 1950.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the two 1946 events by date.

s: At the first sitting of the Constituent Assembly, the number of members who attended was
x: The first sitting, held on 9 December 1946, was attended by 211 members. The Muslim League boycotted the sitting.
tq: Distinguish attendance at the first sitting from the total strength before and after partition.

s: Who served as the temporary President of the Constituent Assembly?
x: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha served as the temporary President because he was the eldest member; the practice was associated with the French constitutional tradition.
tq: Separate the temporary presiding officer from the permanent President and Vice-President.

s:
With reference to the office-bearers of the Constituent Assembly, consider the following statements:

1. H.C. Mukherjee was elected Vice-President on 11 December 1946.
2. V.T. Krishnamachari later also served as Vice-President.
3. B.N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser.
4. G.V. Mavalankar was the Constitutional Adviser.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: H.C. Mukherjee was elected Vice-President, V.T. Krishnamachari later also held that office, and B.N. Rau was Constitutional Adviser. G.V. Mavalankar was the Speaker of the Dominion Legislature.
tq: Reject the swapped office-holder in the final statement.

s: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 transformed the Constituent Assembly into
o: a purely advisory body under the Governor-General
a temporary body without legislative authority
a nominated body functioning only for princely states
a fully sovereign body with constitution-making and legislative functions
x: The Indian Independence Act, 1947 made the Constituent Assembly fully sovereign. It functioned both as the constitution-making body and as the Dominion Legislature, or first Parliament.
tq: Match the Act with the expanded constitutional status and dual functions it created.

s: Which one of the following correctly describes the two roles of the Constituent Assembly after the Indian Independence Act, 1947?
o: Constitution-maker chaired by Rajendra Prasad and Dominion Legislature chaired by G.V. Mavalankar
Constitution-maker chaired by G.V. Mavalankar and Dominion Legislature chaired by Rajendra Prasad
Both roles chaired by B.R. Ambedkar
Both roles chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru
x: Rajendra Prasad chaired the Assembly in its constitution-making role, while G.V. Mavalankar chaired it as the Dominion Legislature.
tq: Keep the two institutional roles and their presiding officers distinct.

s: The Constituent Assembly continued as the Provisional Parliament until
x: The Constituent Assembly continued to function as the Provisional Parliament until 1952.
tq: Distinguish the end of constitution-making from the end of the provisional legislative phase.

s: What was the principal reason for the reduction in the strength of the Constituent Assembly from 389 to 299?
o: Withdrawal of League members from Indian territory after Partition
Removal of women members from the Assembly
x: After Partition, Muslim League members from territories that became part of Pakistan withdrew, reducing the strength from 389 to 299.
tq: Link the numerical change to the political event responsible for it.

s: Which political organisation demanded the dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and its re-election on the basis of adult suffrage?
x: The Socialist Party demanded dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and its re-election through adult suffrage.
tq: Identify the organisation associated with the specific constitutional criticism.

s: Which of the following was NOT a criticism levelled against the Constituent Assembly?
o: It was dominated by lawyers and Hindus.
It was directly elected by universal adult suffrage.
It was not elected on the basis of adult franchise.
It was criticised for being slow in its work.
x: The Constituent Assembly was not directly elected by universal adult suffrage; it was indirectly elected under the Government of India Act, 1935, through a restricted franchise based on factors such as tax, property and education.
tq: Find the statement that reverses the central criticism about the method of election.

s: Vallabhbhai Patel’s remark, “The British element is gone, but they have left mischief behind,” was made in the context of
o: the appointment of the Drafting Committee
x: Patel made the remark while discussing the legacy of separate electorates introduced during British rule.
tq: Associate the quotation with the constitutional issue it criticised.

s: On which date was the Objectives Resolution moved in the Constituent Assembly?
x: Jawaharlal Nehru moved the Objectives Resolution on 13 December 1946.
tq: Separate the date of moving the Resolution from the later date of its adoption.
sec: Objectives Resolution - mover, dates, link to Preamble

s: The Objectives Resolution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on
x: The Objectives Resolution was adopted unanimously on 22 January 1947.
tq: Use the sequence of moving and adopting the Resolution to avoid date reversal.
sec: Objectives Resolution - mover, dates, link to Preamble

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Objectives Resolution:

1. It laid down the philosophy and guiding principles of the Constitution.
2. It was adopted unanimously.
3. Its modified version became the Preamble.
4. It was moved by B.R. Ambedkar.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. The Objectives Resolution was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru, not B.R. Ambedkar.
tq: Use the mover–content–constitutional outcome relationship to reject the swapped name.
sec: Objectives Resolution - mover, dates, link to Preamble

s: The Constituent Assembly constituted under the Cabinet Mission scheme originally consisted of
x: The original Constituent Assembly had 389 members: 296 from British India and 93 from the princely states.
tq: Distinguish the original strength of 389 from the post-Partition strength of 299.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s: Which of the following correctly represents the original composition of the Constituent Assembly?
o: 289 provincial seats, 7 Chief Commissioners’ provinces and 93 princely-state seats
296 provincial seats and 93 nominated seats from British India
292 provincial seats, 4 Chief Commissioners’ provinces and 93 princely-state seats
292 princely-state seats, 4 provincial seats and 93 Chief Commissioners’ seats
x: The 389 seats comprised 296 seats from British India—292 from provinces and 4 from Chief Commissioners’ provinces—and 93 seats from princely states.
tq: Break the total into its component categories before checking the option.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s: Under the Cabinet Mission scheme, approximately how many seats in the Constituent Assembly were allotted for every ten lakh population?
x: The scheme provided approximately one seat in the Constituent Assembly for every ten lakh population.
tq: Identify the population-to-seat ratio rather than confusing it with the community allocation formula.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s:
With regard to the election of members from the provinces, consider the following statements:

1. Provincial seats were divided among General, Muslim and Sikh communities.
2. The division was broadly based on population.
3. Members of each community were elected by all members of the provincial assembly jointly.
4. Proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote was used.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Members of each community were elected by the members of that community in the provincial assembly, not by all members jointly.
tq: Spot the changed electoral constituency in the third statement.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s: Which of the following was the correct distribution of seats won in the July 1946 elections to the Constituent Assembly?
x: In the July 1946 results, the Congress won 208 seats, the Muslim League 73 and other parties won 15 seats.
tq: Preserve the party–seat pairing while eliminating options that exchange the two major parties.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s: Which of the following groups of princely states joined the Constituent Assembly on 28 April 1947?
o: Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa and Udaipur
Bikaner, Jaipur, Junagadh, Patiala, Travancore and Udaipur
Hyderabad, Mysore, Travancore, Kashmir, Baroda and Bikaner
Jaipur, Jodhpur, Hyderabad, Patiala, Rewa and Udaipur
x: The six states that joined on 28 April 1947 were Baroda, Bikaner, Jaipur, Patiala, Rewa and Udaipur.
tq: Use list-based recall and reject options containing states not included in the specified group.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s: Which one of the following statements about the social composition of the Constituent Assembly is correct?
o: It was directly elected by universal adult suffrage and included no women members.
It consisted exclusively of members of the Congress Working Committee.
It was partly elected and partly nominated, and included 15 women members.
It was wholly nominated by the British Government.
x: The Constituent Assembly was partly elected and partly nominated, and it included 15 women members, among them Durgabai Deshmukh, Sarojini Naidu and Hansa Mehta.
tq: Combine the method of constitution with the numerical and representative-composition details.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s: Which of the following pairs of women members of the Constituent Assembly is correctly matched?
o: Durgabai Deshmukh, Sarojini Naidu and Hansa Mehta — women members of the Constituent Assembly
Durgabai Deshmukh, Hansa Mehta and G.V. Mavalankar — women members
Sarojini Naidu, B.N. Rau and Hansa Mehta — women members
Hansa Mehta, K.M. Munshi and Durgabai Deshmukh — women members
x: Durgabai Deshmukh, Sarojini Naidu and Hansa Mehta were among the 15 women members of the Constituent Assembly.
tq: Reject options containing male office-holders substituted for women members.
sec: Composition - Cabinet Mission scheme, election, princely states, women

s:
Arrange the following developments concerning the origin of the idea of a Constituent Assembly in chronological order:

A. The idea was attributed to Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
B. M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly.
C. The Indian National Congress made it an official demand.
D. The idea was accepted in principle in the August Offer.
x: The sequence is 1895, 1934, 1935 and 1940: attribution to Tilak, proposal by M.N. Roy, official INC demand and acceptance in principle through the August Offer.
tq: Anchor the sequence to the four years and arrange them from earliest to latest.

s: Who is generally credited with first putting forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934?
x: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly in 1934. The idea had earlier been attributed to Bal Gangadhar Tilak in 1895 by some sources.
tq: Separate the earlier attribution to Tilak from the specific 1934 formulation by M.N. Roy.

s: In which year did the Indian National Congress make the demand for a Constituent Assembly an official demand?
x: The Indian National Congress adopted the demand for a Constituent Assembly as an official demand in 1935.
tq: Distinguish the year of M.N. Roy’s proposal from the subsequent year of official INC adoption.

s: Jawaharlal Nehru’s 1938 position regarding constitution-making was that the Constitution should be framed by
o: the existing Central Legislative Assembly alone
a body nominated by the British Parliament
the rulers of the princely states
an Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise
x: In 1938, Nehru stated that the Constitution should be framed by an Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise.
tq: Associate the leader and year with the precise democratic method proposed.

s: The demand for a Constituent Assembly was accepted in principle in the August Offer of
x: The demand was accepted in principle in the August Offer of 1940.
tq: Use the chronological progression from INC demand to August Offer to avoid year substitution.

s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Member)
a. B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya
b. N. G. Ranga
c. Durgabai Deshmukh
d. M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar

List-II (Role or association)
i. Peasant leader associated with the Kisan movement
ii. Founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha
iii. Chaired the House Committee
iv. Later became Deputy Speaker and Speaker of the Lok Sabha

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya chaired the House Committee; N. G. Ranga was a peasant leader; Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha; and M. Ananthasayanam Ayyangar later became Deputy Speaker and Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate codes containing a swapped role.
sec: Members from the Andhra region - roles

s: B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was associated with which of the following combinations?
o: President of the Indian National Congress at Calcutta in 1911 and Chairman of the Union Power Committee
President of the Indian National Congress at Belgaum in 1924 and Chairman of the Advisory Committee
President of the Indian National Congress at Lahore in 1929 and Chairman of the Provincial Constitution Committee
President of the Indian National Congress at Jaipur in 1948 and Chairman of the House Committee
x: B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya chaired the House Committee and served as INC President at the Jaipur session in 1948.
tq: Use the person–office and person–session association directly.
sec: Members from the Andhra region - roles

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Some accounts identify P. Ananda Charlu as the first Telugu President of the Indian National Congress.
2. P. Ananda Charlu is associated with the year 1891 in this context.
3. B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya was INC President at Jaipur in 1948.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All three statements are correct: some accounts cite P. Ananda Charlu in 1891, while B. Pattabhi Sitaramayya presided over the INC at Jaipur in 1948.
tq: Separate the alternative historical attribution from the clearly dated Congress presidency.
sec: Members from the Andhra region - roles

s:
Arrange the following events relating to the Andhra demand in chronological order:
A. Andhra was dropped from the Draft Constitution.
B. The Dhar Commission was named.
C. Jawaharlal Nehru accepted the Andhra demand in the Constituent Assembly.

Select the correct sequence.
x: Nehru accepted the Andhra demand on 27 November 1947; Andhra was dropped from the Draft Constitution on 21 February 1948; and the Dhar Commission was named on 17 June 1948.
tq: Fix the earliest and latest dates first, then place the intermediate event.
sec: Members from the Andhra region - roles

s:
With reference to the Andhra demand in the Constituent Assembly, consider the following statements:
1. Nehru accepted the demand on 27 November 1947.
2. Andhra was subsequently dropped from the Draft Constitution on 21 February 1948.
3. The Dhar Commission was named on 17 June 1948.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The Andhra demand was accepted by Nehru in the Assembly on 27 November 1947, omitted from the Draft Constitution on 21 February 1948, and followed by the naming of the Dhar Commission on 17 June 1948.
tq: Check each date independently before selecting the coded combination.
sec: Members from the Andhra region - roles

s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Election of Rajendra Prasad as First President — 24 January 1950
x: The National Song, Vande Mataram, was adopted on 24 January 1950. 27 December 1911 is associated with the first singing of Jana Gana Mana at the Calcutta INC session.
tq: Find the single date that belongs to a different national-symbol event.

s: The National Flag of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on
x: The Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on 22 July 1947.
tq: Distinguish the earlier flag-adoption date from the cluster of January 1950 decisions.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the evolution of the Indian National Flag:
1. Pingali Venkayya designed the tricolour in 1921.
2. He showed the design to Mahatma Gandhi at the AICC session at Bezwada.
3. Gandhi added the charkha to the design.
4. The Constituent Assembly replaced the charkha with the Ashoka Chakra.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: All four statements correctly describe the development of the national flag: Venkayya designed the tricolour in 1921, presented it at Bezwada, Gandhi added the charkha, and the Assembly replaced it with the Ashoka Chakra.
tq: Read the sequence as a design-development chain and test every stage.

s: Who among the following composed Vande Mataram, and in which work does it appear?
x: Vande Mataram was composed by Bankim Chandra Chatterji and appears in Anandamath.
tq: Use the author–work pairing and reject swapped authors or works.

s:
Arrange the following events associated with Vande Mataram in chronological order:
A. Vande Mataram was first sung by Rabindranath Tagore at an INC session.
B. Vande Mataram was composed.
C. Vande Mataram appeared in Anandamath.

Select the correct sequence.
x: Vande Mataram was composed in 1875, appeared in Anandamath in 1882, and was first sung by Tagore at the 1896 INC session.
tq: Arrange the events by their stated years: 1875, 1882 and 1896.

s: Which one of the following statements about Pingali Venkayya is correct?
o: He was born in 1948 at Bhatlapenumarru and was popularly known as Loknayak.
He was born in 1921 at Bezwada and was popularly known as Desabandhu.
He was born in 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru and was popularly known as Jhanda Venkayya.
He was born in 1891 at Jaipur and was popularly known as Andhra Kesari.
x: Pingali Venkayya was born in 1876 at Bhatlapenumarru and is popularly known as Jhanda Venkayya.
tq: Match the commemorated personality with the exact birthplace, year and popular title.

s: The national observance associated with 150 years of Vande Mataram was reported in
x: The national celebration of 150 years of Vande Mataram was reported in October 2025.
tq: Separate a recent anniversary observance from the original composition and adoption dates.

s:
Consider the following statements regarding the reported 2026 amendment to the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act:
1. It reportedly extends to the National Song the protection already given to the National Anthem.
2. The report concerning this amendment was dated 23 August 2026.
3. The amendment concerns the design of the National Flag by Pingali Venkayya.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: The reported amendment extends the protection given to the National Anthem to the National Song, and the report was dated 23 August 2026. It does not concern the design of the National Flag.
tq: Identify the correct subject and date while rejecting a neighbouring national-symbol fact.

s: The Munshi–Ayyangar formula is recalled in connection with Hindi Diwas because it was adopted on
x: The Munshi–Ayyangar formula was adopted on 14 September 1949, a date recalled in connection with Hindi Diwas.
tq: Distinguish the language-related constitutional date from dates connected with Andhra and national symbols.

s: Which one of the following best captures the principal criticism and counter-view concerning the Constituent Assembly?
o: It was criticised because it had no Congress members, although it represented only one political opinion.
It was criticised solely for adopting national symbols before discussing fundamental rights.
It was universally regarded as fully representative and excluded all dissenting views.
It was criticised for representativeness and Congress dominance, but it also included a broad range of views.
x: The Constituent Assembly faced criticism concerning its representativeness and Congress dominance, while its broad inclusion of different views formed an important counter-consideration.
tq: Balance the criticism with the qualifying counter-view rather than choosing an absolute claim.
